mechanism_narrative: MET (RTK with intrinsic kinase domain) and OSMR (type I cytokine receptor lacking intrinsic kinase, signaling via JAK1/2) are forced into proximity by the flexible GS4 linker (~20 Å). MET's kinase transphosphorylates OSMR's JAK-docking sites, while JAK1/2 transphosphorylate MET's multisubstrate docking site (Y1349/Y1356). This bidirectional transphosphorylation enables GRB2-SHC1-GAB1-PIK3R1 signalosome assembly (MAPK/PI3K) AND JAK-STAT3/5 activation simultaneously — a combination not achievable by either receptor alone. PLCG1/2 are sterically excluded because the MET-OSMR co-cluster geometry does not position PLCγ's SH2 domains to bridge the kinase-substrate interface. FRS2/3 and IRS1/2 are excluded because OSMR lacks the juxtamembrane phosphotyrosine motifs required for their docking. The biased output is MAPK↑, PI3K-AKT↑, JAK-STAT3/5↑ with PLCγ-Ca2+↓, producing a transcriptional shift that upregulates muscle structural/contractile genes (young-enriched P2_up signature) and downregulates aged inflammatory/stress immediate-early genes (P1_up signature).
